metadata.note: The Atlantic and Yadkin Railway and its predecessor the Cape Fear and Yadkin Valley Railway, North Carolina. Main line Sanford - Cumnock - Gulf - Siler City - Climax - Greensboro - Stokesdale - Walnut Cove - Rural Hall - Pilot Mountain - Mount Airy (130.0 mi), drawn in three operator eras on identical geometry (Rule 4 split): Cape Fear and Yadkin Valley 1884-1899 (Sanford - Greensboro, opened 1884) and 1888-1899 (Greensboro - Mount Airy, opened 1888); Southern Railway 1899-1916 (Southern took all the stock and operated the line from 13 May 1899); Atlantic and Yadkin 1916-1939 (own operation until the last passenger train, 29 Apr 1939). CF&YV branches: Madison Branch (Stokesdale - Madison) and Factory Branch (Climax - Ramseur), both 1892 [OPEN] - 1895 [OPEN]; Fayetteville - Bennettsville SC 1884-1899 (went to the Wilmington & Weldon / ACL in 1899). Research report: research/branches/atlantic_and_yadkin_railway.txt.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (Overpass, maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-04): ways with old_railway_operator=Southern + note:old_railway_operator='Atlantic and Yadkin' (Yadkin Valley RR / CF Line, abandoned grade, Atlantic and Yadkin Greenway); ACL-tagged track and abandoned grade between Fayetteville and Bennettsville

OpenHistoricalMap (2026-11-04) searched over the lifted stretches; its 'Cape Fear & Yadkin Valley Railway' ways (Greensboro, and Fayetteville - Sanford) were available to the router but the Fayetteville - Sanford one is outside this layer's scope
metadata.operator_split: Main line: CF&YV to 1899 (A&Y's own Feb 15 - May 13 1899 folded in), Southern Railway 1899-1916, Atlantic and Yadkin 1916-1939, identical geometry. Southern's colour pulled programmatically from the 22 existing 'Southern Railway' features. Split year 1916 vs 1917 is a SOURCE CONFLICT (abandonedrails, NAOTC: 1916; Wikipedia, Carolana: 1917); drawn at 1916.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN BOTH ENDS: cfyv-madison-branch 1892-1895 - first and last CONFIRMED years from CF&YV timetables, not known start or end. Opened Dec 1888 (NCRC) or 1890 (ICC); no passenger evidence after the Nov 1895 schedule; branch abandoned 1937-44. Next source: DigitalNC (Greensboro Telegram 1897, Greensboro Patriot, Mount Airy News).
OPEN BOTH ENDS: cfyv-factory-branch 1892-1895 - same evidence and same limits; Ramseur was freight-only by Dec 1951 (Official Guide index dagger), so the true end is 'unknown, before 1951'.
Southern -> A&Y operating split: 1916 (abandonedrails, NAOTC) vs 1917 (Wikipedia, Carolana). Drawn at 1916.
Whether Sanford - Greensboro lost its passenger trains before Greensboro - Mount Airy: every source speaks of the Mount Airy - Sanford train ending in 1939; drawn to 1939 on that basis.
Last-train date: 29 Apr 1939 (NC Museum of History, WVNC) vs Sunday 30 Apr (1939 newspaper, search summary only) vs June 1939 (blog).
Greensboro - Summerfield/Stokesdale probably carried passengers in 1887 (Summerfield marker, snippet only); drawn from 1888.

No Southern-era (1899-1916) or A&Y-era (1916-1939) timetable was read; headway_min for those eras and avg_speed_kmh everywhere are estimates. 'Increased to two trains' after 1900 is undated (NC Museum of History).
Western Railroad (Fayetteville - Egypt, 1860-1879) passenger service - unsourced; not drawn (report block [10], drawable NONE).
metadata.omitted: Not drawn: report block [7] Fayetteville - Sanford and [8] Wilmington - Fayetteville CF&YV eras - wilmington_network.geojson already draws Wilmington - Sanford from 1890 in one unsplit CF&YV/ACL feature (a defect left for a separate PR); block [10] Western Railroad (drawable NONE); freight-only spurs (Gulf - Cape Fear Bluff quarry, Mount Airy - Woodruff and granite quarry spurs, Greensboro - Proximity Mills, Sanford - Aldrich Quarry); the whole A&Y after 1939 (freight only); Mount Airy & Eastern (separate company); the projected Mount Airy - Ore Knob line (never built). Madison and Factory branches are not drawn in the Southern or A&Y eras because no passenger evidence after 1895 was found.

segments.note: Report block [1]. Gulf - Greensboro opened 19 June 1884 (NC Railroad Commission 1st Annual Report 1891, quoted by Carolana; ICC Valuation vol. 37); through service Greensboro - Fayetteville - Bennettsville from 5 Dec 1884 (NCRC). Sanford - Cumnock - Gulf was open earlier (Western RR to Egypt 1860, to Gulf Mar 1879) but no passenger source predates 1884, so nothing earlier is drawn. Through Wilmington - Fayetteville - Sanford - Greensboro - Mt. Airy train in the CF&YV's own printed timetables: daily except Sunday in the Sept 1891/92 and 27 Nov 1892 schedules, daily in the 3 Nov 1895 schedule (receiver John Gill). Ends 1899: receivership 1894, foreclosure 29 Dec 1898, Atlantic and Yadkin in possession 15 Feb 1899, Southern Railway took control and operation 13 May 1899 (ICC). The A&Y's own three months of 1899 are folded into this split. headway_min 1440 = one train each way a day, from the 1891-95 timetables; for 1884-1890 it is an estimate (no timetable read).
sources: Segment-level: start 1884 from NCRC (via Carolana) and ICC; service 1891/92-1895 from three CF&YV timetables (Darlington Herald 21 Sep 1892 and 17 Feb 1893, Florence Daily Times 2 Dec 1895); end 1899 = ICC transfer date to Southern operation.

segments.note: Report blocks [2] and [3]. Built Greensboro - Belew's Creek 1886 and Belew's Creek - Pilot Mountain 1887 (NCRC); open for business at Rural Hall 15 Jan 1888 (WVNC Rails); Greensboro - Mount Airy completed 11 June 1888 (ICC), first passenger train at Mount Airy 20 June 1888 (WVNC; NC Museum of History has a trial run 28 May 1888). Conflict recorded: the Summerfield historical marker says 'first trains: 1887' (seen only as a search snippet) - Greensboro - Summerfield/Stokesdale probably carried passengers in 1887, but 1888 is the first year confirmed for the whole segment, so the drawing starts 1888. Through train Wilmington - Mt. Airy in the 1891/92, 1892 and 1895 CF&YV timetables (Walnut Cove connection with the N&W for Winston-Salem). Ends 1899 on the transfer to Southern operation (ICC, 13 May 1899). headway_min 1440 from the 1891-95 timetables; 1888-90 estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 1888 from ICC (completion 11 Jun 1888) and WVNC Rails (first passenger train 20 Jun 1888, Rural Hall 15 Jan 1888); service 1891/92-1895 from three CF&YV timetables; end 1899 = ICC transfer date.

segments.note: Report block [6] / ownership_split era 2. On 13 May 1899 Southern Railway 'acquired the entire capital stock of the Atlantic and Yadkin and by virtue of this control assumed operation of that portion of the property north of Sanford', operating it 'through stock control without a written agreement' (ICC Valuation vol. 37). Southern, not the A&Y, ran the trains in these years, hence this feature in Southern's colour. Operator split 1916: Southern Railway, which had taken all A&Y stock on 13 May 1899 and 'assumed operation' of the line north of Sanford (ICC), ran the trains until the A&Y was given its own operation. SOURCE CONFLICT: 1916 (abandonedrails.com: 'Southern operated the line until 1916'; NAOTC: 'From Southern ... in 1916'; consistent with the ICC's 1916 valuation date) vs 1917 (Wikipedia: 'considered part of Southern until 1917'; Carolana: 'in 1917 allowed it to run independently'). Split drawn at 1916. Frequency: one train each way daily Mount Airy - Sanford at first; 'a few years after 1900, the service was increased to two trains' (NC Museum of History) - the year of the increase is undated, so headway_min 1440 is kept for the whole span; headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 13 May 1899 from ICC Valuation vol. 37; end 1916 = the operator split (abandonedrails, NAOTC; 1917 per Wikipedia and Carolana - conflict in the note); no Southern-era timetable was read, so the headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Report block [6] / ownership_split era 3. The A&Y ran its own trains from 1916 (Operator split 1916: Southern Railway, which had taken all A&Y stock on 13 May 1899 and 'assumed operation' of the line north of Sanford (ICC), ran the trains until the A&Y was given its own operation. SOURCE CONFLICT: 1916 (abandonedrails.com: 'Southern operated the line until 1916'; NAOTC: 'From Southern ... in 1916'; consistent with the ICC's 1916 valuation date) vs 1917 (Wikipedia: 'considered part of Southern until 1917'; Carolana: 'in 1917 allowed it to run independently'). Split drawn at 1916.) until passenger service ended in 1939: 'Passenger train service for the A & Y came to an end on April 29, 1939' (NC Museum of History; WVNC Rails gives the same date; a 1939 newspaper item seen only in a search summary says the last trip was Sunday 30 April; the bobbyfromnc blog says June 1939 - the year agrees). The sources speak of the Mount Airy - Sanford train, so the Sanford - Greensboro half is taken to end with it; no source dates a separate earlier end for it. The 1924 receivership did not change the operating company. Freight continued after 1939 (the Feb 1952 Official Guide prints Southern Table 60 'Sanford and Mount Airy' as freight service only), and the A&Y merged into Southern on 1 Jan 1950; Rural Hall - Mount Airy is still freight today as the Yadkin Valley Railroad - context only. headway_min 720 = two trains each way, from the Museum's 'increased to two trains' after 1900; whether that held through the A&Y years is unsourced, so it is an estimate. The train's nickname 'Shoofly' is from a blog only.
sources: Segment-level: start 1916 = operator split (abandonedrails, NAOTC; 1917 per Wikipedia/Carolana - conflict in the note); end 1939 from NC Museum of History and WVNC Rails (29 Apr 1939), bobbyfromnc (June 1939); headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Report block [4]. Stokesdale - Rocky Springs - Ellisboro - Madison. [OPEN] BOTH ENDS. 1892 is the first CONFIRMED year and 1895 the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known start or end. The 1891 effective date of the first timetable is an OCR reading and the paper was printed in 1892, so the start is held at 1892; the Nov 1896 printing reprints a schedule dated April 1895, so the end is held at the 3 Nov 1895 effective date. Nothing was found for 1896-1939 (DigitalNC, the obvious next source, was unreachable). Do not extend either end without evidence. Evidence: No.17 Madison 7:00 - Stokesdale 7:55 - Greensboro 9:10am, daily except Sunday (CF&YV schedule OCR-dated Sept 10 1891, Darlington Herald 21 Sep 1892); No.16 Greensboro 10:15am - Madison 12:30pm and return (27 Nov 1892 schedule); Nos. 15/16 MIXED, daily except Sunday, through-worked Ramseur - Climax - Greensboro - Stokesdale - Madison (3 Nov 1895 schedule). Opening conflict: Dec 1888 (NCRC) vs 1890 (ICC 'construction completed'). The branch was abandoned 'sometime between 1937 and 1944' (abandonedrails) - an abandonment bracket, not a passenger end. Not the N&W's Madison station, a different railroad through the same town. headway_min 1440 = one (mixed) train each way, daily except Sunday, from the timetables.
sources: Segment-level: 1892 and 1895 are the first and last CONFIRMED years from the CF&YV's printed timetables (Darlington Herald 21 Sep 1892 and 17 Feb 1893; Florence Daily Times 2 Dec 1895; reprint 28 Nov 1896). Both ends are open.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 56.13 mi against 58.1 mi documented (Fowler NC line 51: Fayetteville - Parkton 13.1 + Parkton - Bennettsville 45.0; Wikipedia's CF&YV table 58.1). Straight-line legs: CSX S of Fayetteville - CF&YV old grade Fayetteville end 1.96 mi; CF&YV old grade Hope Mills N - Hope Mills 0.7 mi; CSX SW of Hope Mills - Red Springs line W of Parkton 4.14 mi (total 6.8 mi). ERA-ALIGNMENT: the CF&YV's own Fayetteville - Hope Mills - west-of-Parkton line was abandoned in 1899, so this deliberately avoids the later ACL route through Parkton where it can: Fayetteville - 2 mi south on the CSX/ACL track (a later alignment, drawn for want of the lifted original); a 1.96 mi chord to the north end of an abandoned ACL-tagged grade parallel to and west of the CSX, which is followed 2.6 mi to Hope Mills (taken to be the original CF&YV grade; identification by position only); a 0.7 mi chord back onto the CSX at Hope Mills; Hope Mills - 2.4 mi south-west on the CSX track (LATER ALIGNMENT - whether the 1884 line shared this alignment is unknown); then a 4.1 mi chord standing in for the lifted original line to the Red Springs line west of Parkton (no mapped grade in OSM or OHM). Parkton - Lumber Bridge - Red Springs - Maxton - McColl - Bennettsville on ACL-tagged track and abandoned grade (8.4 mi on untagged rail).  Waypoints within 1.0 km.

segments.note: Report block [9]. Fayetteville - Hope Mills - Lumber Bridge - Red Springs - Maxton - McColl - Bennettsville SC. Opened to Maxton 1 Aug 1884 and through to Bennettsville 5 Dec 1884 (NCRC, via Carolana); the 10.5 mi state line - Bennettsville was the South Carolina Pacific, leased by the CF&YV from Jan 1885 for 30 years. Nos. 3/4 Fayetteville - Bennettsville daily except Sunday (27 Nov 1892 schedule) and daily (3 Nov 1895 schedule). Ends 1899: on 13 May 1899 the lines south of Sanford were conveyed to the Wilmington & Weldon (Atlantic Coast Line from 1900) (ICC); ACL-era service is the ACL layer's business and is not drawn here. The original Fayetteville - Hope Mills - west-of-Parkton line was 'abandoned in 1899' when trains were moved onto the ACL's 1892 Fayetteville cutoff via Parkton (Carolana). headway_min 1440 from the 1892 and 1895 timetables; 1884-91 estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 1884 from NCRC (via Carolana); service 1892 and 1895 from the CF&YV timetables (Darlington Herald 17 Feb 1893; Florence Daily Times 2 Dec 1895); end 1899 = ICC transfer to the Wilmington & Weldon.
